what: the parked recipe follow-ups, run after the AG-Bench: threads 4/6/8 A/B with the same fixed prompt classes, 2 runs each, fresh-prefill, server-reported rates
method_note: harness now committed as benchmarks/measure-decode.sh; acceptance = accepted/drafted tokens, mean_len = predicted/verify-count (reproduces prior conventions: TC d2 0.995/2.99, A3B d4 0.774/4.09)
verdict: run-1 values are cold (page cache still streaming the 17GB mmapped expert band from SSD); run-2 is the steady state. The sweep revealed the true steady state: fully-warmed short-context decode is ~20 tok/s on BOTH prompt classes — 2.3x the 9.29/8.52 of the main bench session (measured mid-session under real memory pressure; deep agent turns still fit under it). threads 4/6/8 are indistinguishable within run-to-run noise in steady state; the recipe's threads 6 (physical cores) stays.

the MoE-with-CPU-experts class DOES fit this card (4.57 GB for a 35B) and its MTP head accepts at the same rates as the family (0.77/0.61, mean 3.4-4.1) — but with 16 GB RAM the expert band caps operational decode at 9.3/8.5 falling to 1.5 in deep agent turns, so the model spends 14+ minutes on tasks the 4B clears in 20 s. Verdict: viable to RUN on this card (first 35B here at all), not viable as a working slot while RAM is 16 GB; would become the smart-slot if the machine ever grows memory. Also: llama.cpp w/ CUDA has no MoE CPU-expert ping-pong penalty on this run — the hybrid attn KV stays tiny, specs do what they promise.

what: --load-mode none (the loader warning's own recommendation when using tensor overrides) was served once. RESULT: the box FROZE — systemd-oomd 'Marked vicinae.service for killing due to memory pressure 89.67% > 50% for >20s' followed by a kernel page-fault storm (do_fault/__handle_mm_fault) and desktop lockup; hard reboot required. --load-mode none disables mmap and force-reads the ENTIRE 17.4GB model into 16GB RAM.
verdict: BANNED on this machine, permanently. Any future serve of >12GB models on 16GB RAM must use mmap (default). All subsequent serves tonight run with a cgroup guard (--memory 13g) so a bad config dies in its container instead of taking the desktop down.
